questions.prompt: The first person to observe living microorganisms, using a single-lens microscope, was
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek described living "animalcules" in the 1670s. Hooke drew the cells of cork with a compound microscope in 1665 but did not see living microbes. Pasteur and Koch worked two centuries later.

questions.prompt: Louis Pasteur's swan-neck flask experiments disproved
questions.explanation: Broth in a swan-neck flask stayed sterile until the neck was broken, showing microbes come from existing microbes in the air. The experiment supports the germ theory rather than disproving it.

questions.prompt: The fourth of Koch's postulates requires that the microbe be

options.text: killed by an antibiotic before inoculation
grown only in living tissue cells
re-isolated from the experimentally infected host and shown to be the same organism
found in every healthy person in the community

questions.explanation: After the pure culture causes disease in a healthy susceptible host, the same agent must be recovered from that host. Recovering it from healthy people would contradict the first postulate.

questions.prompt: Which of these organisms has no membrane-bound nucleus?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes: their DNA lies in a nucleoid, not inside a nuclear membrane. Yeast, amoeba and Chlamydomonas are eukaryotes with true nuclei.

questions.prompt: The thick cell wall layer that holds the crystal violet-iodine complex in Gram-positive bacteria is mainly
questions.explanation: Gram-positive walls have a thick peptidoglycan layer. Lipopolysaccharide belongs to the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria. Chitin is a fungal wall component and cellulose a plant one.

questions.prompt: In the Gram stain, the step that removes the crystal violet from Gram-negative cells is the use of
questions.explanation: Alcohol dissolves the outer membrane and washes the dye complex out of the thin peptidoglycan of Gram-negative cells. Safranin is the counterstain applied afterwards.

questions.prompt: After a correct Gram stain, Gram-negative bacteria appear
questions.explanation: They lose the crystal violet at the decolorising step and then take up the safranin counterstain, so they look pink. Gram-positive cells keep the crystal violet and look purple.

questions.prompt: Bacteria multiply mainly by
questions.explanation: One cell replicates its DNA and divides into two equal daughter cells. Prokaryotes have no spindle, so mitosis and meiosis do not occur in them.

questions.prompt: A virus contains

options.text: either DNA or RNA, but not both

questions.explanation: Viral genomes are one kind of nucleic acid. Viruses have no ribosomes or mitochondria and depend on host cells for synthesis.

questions.prompt: Viruses are most suitably measured in
questions.explanation: Most viruses are about 20 to 300 nm. Bacteria are usually measured in micrometres, which is about a thousand times larger.

questions.prompt: Laboratory media and instruments are normally sterilised in an autoclave at

options.text: 121 degrees C for 15 minutes at 15 psi
100 degrees C for 30 minutes at normal pressure

questions.explanation: Steam under pressure at 121 degrees C kills spores. Boiling at 100 degrees C does not kill spores reliably, and 72 degrees C for 15 seconds is milk pasteurisation.

questions.prompt: Agar, used to solidify culture media, is obtained from
questions.explanation: Agar is a polysaccharide extracted from red algae. Few microbes digest it, so it stays solid. Starch and yeast extract do not form a firm gel.

questions.prompt: MacConkey agar is described as
questions.explanation: Bile salts and crystal violet inhibit Gram-positive bacteria (selective) and lactose with neutral red shows lactose fermenters as pink colonies (differential).

questions.prompt: The cell wall of fungi contains
questions.explanation: Chitin gives fungal walls their strength. Peptidoglycan is bacterial, and cellulose is the main component of plant walls.

questions.prompt: In a binomial name such as Escherichia coli, the first word is the
questions.explanation: The first word is the genus and is capitalised. The second word is the species epithet and is written in lower case. Family and strain are not part of a binomial.

questions.prompt: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin from a mould of the genus
questions.explanation: In 1928 Fleming saw bacterial growth inhibited around a Penicillium colony. Aspergillus, Rhizopus and Mucor are other common moulds but not the source of penicillin.

questions.prompt: Microorganisms that live on or in a healthy body without causing disease are called
questions.explanation: Normal flora are the resident microbes of skin, gut and mucosa. Vectors carry pathogens and fomites are contaminated objects.

questions.prompt: A microscope has a 10x eyepiece and a 100x oil immersion objective. The total magnification is
questions.explanation: Total magnification is the product of the eyepiece and the objective, 10 times 100 equals 1000.

questions.prompt: Immersion oil is used with the 100x objective mainly to

options.text: reduce light loss and improve resolution

questions.explanation: Oil has about the same refractive index as glass, so light is not bent away from the lens. This gives a brighter, sharper image.

questions.prompt: A genus of bacteria that forms endospores is
questions.explanation: Bacillus and Clostridium form endospores. The other genera do not form them.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a feature of prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria. The nucleoid, 70S ribosomes and plasma membrane are all present in them.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a eukaryotic microorganism?
questions.explanation: Candida is a yeast, a fungus. Treponema, Vibrio and Mycoplasma are bacteria.

questions.prompt: A student sees pink rod-shaped cells after a Gram stain. The organism is best reported as
questions.explanation: Pink means Gram-negative and the shape is a rod. Gram-positive organisms would be purple.

questions.prompt: Mycoplasma is unusual among bacteria because it
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall, so penicillin, which targets wall synthesis, does not act on it, and the cells have no fixed shape.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a protozoan?
questions.explanation: Plasmodium is a single-celled eukaryotic parasite. Staphylococcus is a bacterium, Aspergillus a fungus and Hepatitis B a virus.

questions.prompt: Prions are infectious agents made of
questions.explanation: Prions are misfolded proteins with no nucleic acid. They cause diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy.

questions.prompt: Which method is the best way to obtain a pure culture from a mixed sample?
questions.explanation: Streaking spreads cells so that single cells grow into separate colonies, which are then picked and subcultured. Staining and hanging drop only observe.

questions.prompt: A group of cells that arise from a single parent cell on a solid medium is called a
questions.explanation: A colony is a visible mass of cells descended from one cell or a clump of cells.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the best definition of a pathogen?

options.text: A microorganism that can cause disease

questions.explanation: A pathogen damages the host. Many soil and skin microbes are harmless.

questions.prompt: Joseph Lister's contribution to microbiology and medicine was

options.text: the invention of the electron microscope
the use of carbolic acid (phenol) as an antiseptic in surgery

questions.explanation: Lister applied phenol to wounds and instruments to cut surgical infection in the 1860s. Pasteur developed the rabies vaccine and Fleming found penicillin.

questions.prompt: Edward Jenner is remembered for

options.text: developing the smallpox vaccine using cowpox

questions.explanation: In 1796 Jenner showed that cowpox inoculation protected against smallpox. Koch isolated the tuberculosis bacillus in 1882.

questions.prompt: The bacterium Escherichia coli is about 2 micrometres long. This length expressed in nanometres is
questions.explanation: One micrometre is 1000 nm, so 2 micrometres is 2000 nm.

questions.prompt: Viruses can reproduce outside a living host cell if given enough nutrients.
questions.explanation: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites. They have no ribosomes or metabolism of their own, so they replicate only inside living host cells.

questions.prompt: The cell wall of bacteria contains peptidoglycan.
questions.explanation: Peptidoglycan is the characteristic structural polymer of bacterial walls. Archaea and eukaryotes lack it.

questions.prompt: Assertion: Gram-negative bacteria lose the crystal violet during the Gram stain. Reason: The alcohol step dissolves their outer membrane and the thin peptidoglycan cannot hold the dye complex.

options.text: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
The assertion is true but the reason is false
The assertion is false but the reason is true
Both the assertion and the reason are false

questions.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: the outer membrane is damaged by alcohol and the thin wall leaks the dye.
